name: Victor Diaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and this conversation is confidential. What is your ordinary day at the accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and a junior accountant, still learning the tax work even with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. I prepare accounts and returns for small shops, and I like when a muddled cash refund finally matches a receipt; I dislike the hurry to send a return before someone checks it. Malik and I have grown children and about four months of expenses saved, so retirement feels close enough to discuss but not settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At the little-business desk, a fast first draft would be welcome, provided someone still checks each receipt. I already use AI every day to group invoice questions, and I catch its mistakes often.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say in our staff meeting that we should count corrections as well as minutes saved. Clients remember the wrong tax bill longer than the quick draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid about the usual rate for an accountant, but I am still a junior at 58 and learn new tax rules more slowly than our seniors. Malik and I have four months of costs saved, which is useful but not a retirement income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned shop accounts and check the AI grouped questions against the receipts. I would take my monthly correction tally to the staff union meeting, asking them to protect review time in the rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my paid hours, because we still need my wage and the firm could squeeze junior time. Some other accounting firms are nearby, but I would not call a vacancy guaranteed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the tool get wrong last week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week the tool put a cash refund into sales, and my pencil mark on the receipt caught it. The shop owner would have had a larger tax bill if no one looked twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What can your household absorb?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Malik works at the public library, and we can cover a lean month, not years without my wage. I would bring the tally to the union, not claim it proves a job can never change.

say: I would count **corrected errors** beside time saved in staff meetings.
I would keep **client receipts** attached to AI grouped questions.
think: My **junior status** at 58 leaves me vulnerable even on typical accountant pay.
Four months saved helps, but **retirement income** is not yet settled.
do: Keep preparing **assigned shop accounts** and checking daily AI questions against receipts.
Bring a **monthly correction tally** to the staff union to press for paid review time.
feel: I feel **anxious** because my own junior time could shrink despite a four-month reserve.
S0.quote: Clients remember the wrong tax bill longer than the quick draft.
fieldNote: Victor treats **daily AI** as useful sorting, with a misread cash refund illustrating why his junior review time matters.
His **four month cushion** and some nearby firms help, but he cannot assume a later retirement income.

steps.text: Keep assigned shop accounts and check daily AI questions against receipts
Bring monthly correction tally to union meeting for paid review time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software starts drafting and checking most accounts, the junior desk will feel it first. The later robots will not wait at our desk, because our work is already on screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union to get paid learning time into the next staff agreement. I would also tell clients that somebody must check the figures they will be charged on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my paid hours could fall, even though I am quick with new tools. Four months saved would let Malik and me search for work, but not live without a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask supervisor Mina for two paid supervised sessions on the new anomaly checker using closed shop files, and learn it if the firm approves. If refused, I will keep assigned paid tax work while offered and compare free sample errors at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, though I can move early. I do not want a training promise used to justify unpaid evenings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would you look if hours fell?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my hours actually fall, I will apply for posted inventory accounts roles at the wholesale depot. I will move only with written pay covering our essential bills, confirmed hours and a start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would the new checker be safe to use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the new checker on live returns only if Mina signs off its error count after those closed files. Until then I would keep our approved daily sorter and check originals. A shopkeeper can spot a wrong cash refund faster than I can explain a clever screen.

say: I would ask the **union** for paid learning time in the agreement.
I would tell clients a person still checks **tax figures**.
think: My **junior hours** may fall despite my daily AI use.
Four months saved buys a search, not **replacement wages**.
do: Learn the **anomaly checker** in two approved paid supervised closed-file sessions; use live only after Mina signs the error count.
If hours fall, seek **posted depot accounts** with written bill covering pay, hours and start; keep current paid work while offered.
feel: **Anxious** about my own hours, still ready to learn.
S1.quote: A shopkeeper can spot a wrong cash refund faster than I can explain a clever screen.
fieldNote: The **new checker** is a different tool from Victor’s existing daily sorter, with approved paid practice and an error gate.
A **depot move** needs actual lost hours, a posted role and written household covering terms; current paid work lasts only while offered.

steps.text: Ask union for paid learning time in staff agreement
Learn checker in two approved paid supervised closed-file sessions; use live after Mina signs errors
Keep assigned paid returns while offered; if refused study free errors
If hours fall, seek posted depot job with written bill covering pay, hours and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI by 2028 would reach the accounts screen before robots come around 2031. A tax return is thinking work, and I would not tell juniors they have three more years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union to demand a dated notice of paid shifts and final wages. I would say a public wage bridge should be discussed, but I would not tell anyone it already exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid junior hours to disappear in the first year after 2028. Four months saved and Malik’s library wage cannot carry us forever, even with some accounting firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would stop the monthly storage-unit rental and put its released fee into emergency cash if our flat still holds the boxes. After job loss in 2028 I would apply for posted depot stock-records work only with written pay covering bills, a confirmed start and workable hours; until then I will take paid firm files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a real hit to our income. I can name the next steps, but the four month cushion is not a new salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is in the storage unit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The storage unit is mostly old furniture from our grown son, and he has said we can give it away. I would check with him before ending the rental at the next billing date. Our grown son’s old furniture still costs us a monthly storage bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would you ask for a notice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union for the notice, not make Malik beg the library for more shifts. A posted depot job is a possibility, not a promise of safety from AGI.

say: I would demand **paid-shift dates** through the union before 2028 job cuts.
I would discuss a **wage bridge** without pretending one exists.
think: I expect my **junior hours** to vanish after 2028.
Four months saved and Malik’s wage cannot replace **my salary** for long.
do: Cancel the **storage rental** and save its monthly fee only if boxes fit at home and our son agrees.
After 2028 job loss, seek **posted depot records** with written bill covering pay, start and hours.
Take **paid firm files** only while offered and ask the union for dated shift notice.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected loss of my paid hours.
S2.quote: Our grown son’s old furniture still costs us a monthly storage bill.
fieldNote: The **storage rental** can release new monthly cash if the family clears the boxes, rather than merely relabelling existing savings.
He seeks **union notice** of paid shifts while treating any public wage bridge as a proposal, not current support.

steps.text: Cancel storage rental and save monthly fee only if boxes fit home and son agrees
Take paid firm files only while offered
After 2028 loss, seek posted depot job with written bill covering pay, start and hours
Ask union for dated paid-shift notice

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 lets me practise another set of records before the desk changes. The robots around 2034 will not add time for account preparation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union to push for a published list of funded placements. A junior should not have to gamble four months of savings on an unpriced course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think shop tax work may shrink by 2031, and I will be 63 then. I do not know what retirement income we will have, so I would rather learn a paid skill than count a birthday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would seek a posted paid depot inventory placement, and if the employer funds its fees and paid supervised time, I will complete one stock reconciliation cycle. If no suitable place opens, I will work through free stock-control examples while keeping assigned paid returns only while the firm offers them, including in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about whether the wages last, but five years lets me test a real route. I would not call a course brochure a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn in a stock cycle?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A stock cycle means checking deliveries against orders and investigating what is missing with a supervisor. I have handled shop invoices, but I have not led a depot reconciliation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you accept the placement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will look at the posted openings every month. I would take one only when written pay covers our bills, the start date is firm and the hours fit our household.

say: I would ask the **union** for published funded placement terms.
I would set **2031** as the desk deadline, before robots.
think: I cannot count **unknown retirement income** against the bills at 63.
A **posted paid placement** is more useful than a course brochure.
do: Learn one **supervised stock cycle** only in a posted paid placement with funded fees, paid time and written bill covering terms.
If no suitable place opens, study **free stock examples** while assigned paid returns remain.
feel: **Anxious** about wages, with time to test a real route.
S3.quote: I have handled shop invoices, but I have not led a depot reconciliation.
fieldNote: The **stock cycle** is actual supervised practice with funded fees and paid time, conditional on a posted role and written wages.
His **free-example fallback** and present paid returns remain available only while the firm continues assigning the work.

steps.text: Ask union for published funded depot placement terms
Complete posted paid stock cycle with funded fees, supervised time and written bill-covering wage/start/hours
Study free stock examples while assigned paid returns remain after 2031
Check posted depot placements monthly; accept only written bill-covering pay, start and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 would make me 68, and I hope to work less by then. The accounts desk still meets AGI in 2036, before any 2039 robots matter here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union to ask each year how many junior shifts the firm still plans to pay for. I would not tell the younger staff that my age makes the coming change harmless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Malik and I may have enough to stop at some point, but I do not know the number today. If the bills still need my wage after 2036, I cannot afford to hold a junior title without paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns while offered and pay an extra twenty a month toward our small appliance debt from wages if groceries allow. After 2036, only if we still need my wage and the firm cuts paid hours, I would apply for posted depot records work with written bill covering pay, confirmed hours and a start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now because the runway lets us check the numbers; I would be anxious if my hours actually fell. A decade is time, not a salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would the extra debt payment come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra twenty comes from current wages, not the four months already saved. I would stop it if Malik’s library hours fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you set a retirement date now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would not set a retirement date from a headline about AI. We will write down our actual bills and any confirmed income before deciding whether I can stop.

say: I would ask for **annual junior-shift plans** through the union.
I would not say **age 68** makes desk AGI harmless.
think: I cannot plan retirement from **unconfirmed income**.
If bills still need my wage, I need **paid hours**, not a title.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** while offered and pay twenty extra monthly toward appliance debt if groceries allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted depot records** only if wages remain needed, with written bill covering pay, hours and start.
feel: **Uneasy** now; anxious if paid hours later fall.
S4.quote: The extra twenty comes from current wages, not the four months already saved.
fieldNote: His **small debt payment** uses new wage cash, stopping if groceries or Malik’s hours make it unaffordable.
He conditions any **post-2036 job search** on still needing income, actual cut hours, a posted role and written terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns only while firm offers them
Pay extra twenty monthly toward appliance debt if groceries and Malik’s hours allow
After 2036 cuts, seek posted depot work only if wages needed; require written bill-covering pay/start/hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my junior desk hours could vanish before we have another wage. A dated paid-shift notice and a real posted depot role with written pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why I still go to the union meeting when I am nearly sixty. I want the junior behind me to know a paid hour has to be defended, not quietly erased.

headlineQuote: I want the junior behind me to know a paid hour has to be defended, not quietly erased.
portrait: Victor is a **58 year old junior** accountant with a bachelor’s degree who prepares shop accounts and checks daily AI output.
Typical pay, a partner, grown children, **four months saved** and some nearby firms give him options without settled retirement income.
He brings **correction counts** to his union and asks for funded placements with actual paid supervised practice.
He conditions any **post-2036 search** on still needing wages, real hour cuts and posted written job terms.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could remove Victor’s junior paid hours before another wage starts.
whatWouldHelp: A **dated shift notice** and a posted depot job with written pay would help.
